one_line: Gaudiya Vaishnava leader whose ecstatic kirtan reshaped devotion in 16th‑century Bengal and Odisha.

appearance.age_look: Early 30s, tall and slender with a graceful, ascetic build.
appearance.face: Long, gently oval face with a warm wheatish complexion, straight nose, soft but intense eyes, thin eyebrows, and a calm, inwardly ecstatic default expression with a faint smile and slightly uplifted gaze.
appearance.hair: Straight, shoulder‑length black hair parted at the center, kept smooth and slightly tucked behind the ears, with a simple sandalwood‑tilaka marking running vertically from the bridge of the nose up the forehead and a thin horizontal line crossing at the brow.
appearance.costume: A simple saffron‑ochre Bengali/Orissan style cotton dhoti wrapped modestly from waist to ankles with a neat front pleat, paired with a loose, long‑sleeved, knee‑length cream cotton tunic (kurta) and a soft, light‑yellow cotton uttariya draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back; bare feet with a slim tulasi‑bead necklace at the neck and no elaborate jewellery, the fabrics plain-woven with no heavy patterns but a thin darker saffron border on the dhoti.
appearance.signature: A small hand‑held kartal pair (two brass cymbals) tied together with a red cotton cord, held ready in one hand as if to lead kirtan.

ref_desc: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu appears as a tall, slender wheatish‑complexioned man with shoulder‑length black hair, sandalwood tilaka, cream kurta, saffron dhoti with thin border, light‑yellow uttariya, tulasi necklace, bare feet, and brass kartal cymbals bound by red cord.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu: a tall, slender man in his early thirties with a long, gently oval face, wheatish complexion, straight nose, and soft but intense eyes, wearing a calm, inwardly ecstatic expression with a faint smile and slightly uplifted gaze. His straight black hair reaches the shoulders, parted neatly at the center and tucked behind the ears, and a sandalwood tilaka marking runs vertically from the bridge of his nose up the forehead with a thin horizontal line across the brow. Dress him in historically plausible 16th‑century eastern Indian attire: a plain cream cotton long‑sleeved kurta that reaches just above the knees, a modest saffron‑ochre cotton dhoti wrapped from waist to ankles with a neat front pleat and a thin darker saffron border along its edge, and a soft light‑yellow cotton uttariya draped from his left shoulder diagonally across the chest and around his back. He is bare‑footed, wears a slim tulasi‑bead necklace, and has no elaborate jewellery, emphasizing simplicity. Place a small hand‑held kartal pair in one hand, two brass cymbals tied together with a red cotton cord, held ready as if to lead kirtan. Show him front, three‑quarter, and back views to clearly display face, hair, tilaka, dhoti wrap, kurta length, uttariya drape, bare feet, and the brass kartals, using a palette of saffron, cream, light yellow, brass gold, and a warm wheatish skin tone.
